newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ Bank shares continue record run.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ Bank shares continue record run.

text.p: Shares in the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd continued to gain ground on Monday, reaching a record and intraday high of A$7.28 as investors continued to buy into the high-yielding bank sector.

"The banks have been strong, really, for weeks," said director of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale. The attraction of bank stocks, already the most profitable sector on the market, increased in a low inflation environment, he added.
"I think the market switches attention to the prospect of a longer than expected low inflation, low growth environment where the banks obviously stand out."
The rise has also allowed some traders to resurrect the well-worn rumour that Hongkong Bank of Australia, a unit of HSBC Holdings Ltd, was about to bid for ANZ.
"I think it is most unlikely," said Graham Maloney, the Melbourne-based banking analyst at Macquarie Equities.

"They (HSBC) have very strong organic growth in south-east Asia and they haven't got quite the mass they want in the U.S.. So given they have strong growth without buying ANZ, and they have a need to expand their U.S. operations, it is my belief they are more likely to acquire in the U.S. than they are here."
Others also demurred, saying there appeared to be limited scope for rationalisation benefits.

"It is not an impossibility, but the difficulty is there is a very strong overlap between the existing Asian operations and the emerging countries between the two organisations where there does not seem to be a great potential for some rationalisation," said Alistair Hunter, banking analyst at J.B. Were.

Hunter noted the focus on ANZ Bank in the perennial speculation but said that if HSBC was interested in local acquisitions, then all of the major banks offered some attraction, depending on what HSBC was looking for.
"There is a bit of everything in any one of them," he said.
"So I don't think the market should get too carried away with saying there is only one option if that is what they are wanting to do," he said.
ANZ shares closed seven cents higher at A$7.23 on turnover of 4.64 million shares.
